plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. Bidding above value risks overpaying if I win against a high second bid; bidding below value risks losing profitable wins. Since values are drawn independently and this is a one-shot round, I have no additional information about opponents beyond the uniform distribution, so truthful bidding remains optimal.

This is a second-price auction with independent private values. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly your true value, regardless of what others do. Bidding your value ensures: if you win, you pay the second-highest bid (which is less than your value, guaranteeing non-negative profit), and if you lose, it's because someone else valued it more than you did. There's no benefit to shading up or down from true value in a second-price auction. My value is $33, so I'll bid $33.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction), where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others bid. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding my true value of $31 maximizes my expected profit - I won't overpay since I only pay what the second-highest bidder bid, and I ensure I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids while never paying more than my value.
